rapport_notes: Friendly, patient, clear tone; good humor ('Great, king'); handled customer confusion about 15-min billing well with repeated clarification.
process_discipline_notes: Rep asked 'Does that make sense or do you have questions?' after the billing explanation but did not hold silence—immediately continued with 'Let me see and the way the clock works,' creating no space for customer to pause.

evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Not asked or mentioned anywhere in call
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: if the TV is currently mounted, we can also help you dismounted' and 'after that we prorate every fifteen minutes' (this is the 15-min increment credit for finishing early)
evidence_quotes.no_communication: No mention of day-before call, named crew lead, or inbox updates
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor_partial: I think this will just be within the minimum of two and a half hours.' — gives the frame (minimum 2.5 hrs) but does not anchor to a typical range for this move size, nor personalize to floor/logistics dynamically
evidence_quotes.no_save_your_ass_full: Rep does not deliver the 'we commit to the rate' experience framing, the 'estimate is a window' disclosure, the self-prep tip, or the 'does that feel fair?' close with silence
evidence_quotes.no_close_rate_lock: No mention of rate locking at booking
evidence_quotes.no_explicit_ask: Rep offers tentative scheduling but never asks 'would you like our help with your move?' or an explicit close ask; customer initiates the booking request ('can I put down for that')

top_strength: Rep proactively identified the customer's TV as a key concern, delivered a specific damage-protection solution (58" TV bag at no extra cost, wrapping), and earned trust by addressing the customer's stated worry head-on.
coaching_note: Never asked who's coming (Meet Your Mover differentiator), never delivered On-Time Guarantee or Communication info, and abandoned the close—customer had to ask to book; next call, hold silence after open-ended questions, cover all four differentiators in either Stage 1 or Stage 2, and always end with an explicit ask and rate-lock confirmation.
